s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic unilateral eyelid swelling with discharge
salient_findings: 2-year history of swelling of the right upper eyelid
Immovable scarlike node on the right upper eyelid
Ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus on MRI
key_facts: 52-year-old Japanese woman
2-year history of swelling of the right upper eyelid
Pus discharge for 10 months
No trauma to the head
Otherwise healthy
No fever, headache, or nasal discharge
Immovable scarlike node on the right upper eyelid
Node size: 11 × 7 mm
High signal on T2-weighted MRI
Ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus
Opacification of the right frontal, ethmoid, and maxillary sinuses on CT
Expansion of the right frontal and ethmoid sinuses
Mild inflammatory infiltrate with fibrosis on histopathology
Lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate with few eosinophils

raw.syndrome_frame: Chronic unilateral eyelid swelling with discharge
salient_findings: 2-year history of swelling of the right upper eyelid
Immovable scarlike node on the right upper eyelid
Ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus on MRI
key_facts: 52-year-old Japanese woman
2-year history of swelling of the right upper eyelid
Pus discharge for 10 months
No trauma to the head
Otherwise healthy
No fever, headache, or nasal discharge
Immovable scarlike node on the right upper eyelid
Node size: 11 × 7 mm
High signal on T2-weighted MRI
Ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus
Opacification of the right frontal, ethmoid, and maxillary sinuses on CT
Expansion of the right frontal and ethmoid sinuses
Mild inflammatory infiltrate with fibrosis on histopathology
Lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate with few eosinophils

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including a 2-year history of swelling of the right upper eyelid with pus discharge, along with imaging findings of opacification and expansion of the right frontal, ethmoid, and maxillary sinuses, and histopathology showing mild inflammatory infiltrate with fibrosis, are most consistent with chronic sinusitis.

rejected.label: orbital cellulitis
rejected.why: While orbital cellulitis could explain some symptoms, the lack of fever, headache, or other signs of acute infection, and the chronic nature of the symptoms, make it less likely.

rejected.label: conjunctivitis
rejected.why: Conjunctivitis typically presents with eye redness, itching, and discharge, which are not the primary symptoms in this case.

rejected.label: sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Sarcoidosis can cause sinus and eye symptoms, but the histopathology did not show non-caseating granulomas, which are characteristic of sarcoidosis.

rejected.label: embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma
rejected.why: The histopathology did not show any sign of malignancy, making this diagnosis unlikely.
